---
name: current-state-docs-no-history
description: Living/generated docs (data-access maps, dependency graph, section invariants, auth inventory) document CURRENT state only — no move/migration history, no "new this sweep", no PR archaeology, no generated-by boilerplate.
---

**Living and generated docs describe what IS, never how it got that way.** No "moved from
`src/Humans.Application/...` at G5 (#866, PR #1223)", no "peeled #1234", no "new this sweep",
no "found by coverage-verify audit (date)", no "used to be / no longer", and no
"Regenerated by /freshness-sweep" header boilerplate — regeneration mechanics live in
`freshness-catalog.yml`, not in every output file.

**Why:** History is what git and PRs are for. Provenance narrative bloats every regenerated
file, goes stale the moment the next refactor lands, and burns tokens for every agent that
loads the doc (Peter, 2026-08-18, on `data-access.md`: "It exists to document current state").

**How to apply:**

- A date or PR reference is allowed only when it marks a **live pending item** (e.g. "drop
  after prod soak, #832") — never as provenance for a shipped state.
- When regenerating a doc that carries history narrative, delete the narrative; when writing
  a new one, start from the current code and say nothing about predecessors.
- Dated design records (`docs/superpowers/`, `src/Sections/*/Docs/20*.md`) are exempt —
  they are history by design.
